result:
Refactored `src/click/_termui_impl.py`'s pager stream handling: removed `_has_binary_buffer`/`_BufferedTextPagerStream`, and turned `MaybeStripAnsi` from an `io.TextIOWrapper` subclass (which required unwrapping a stream's raw `.buffer` and rewrapping it, plus a `detach()` dance to avoid closing borrowed streams) into a plain composition wrapper applied uniformly to every pager backend's stream. All backends (`_pipepager`, `_tempfilepager`, `_nullpager`) now yield a simple `(stream, color)` pair instead of `(stream, encoding, color)`, since the encoding was only ever needed to reconstruct the old rewrapped `TextIOWrapper`.

This also fixed a real inconsistency: previously, ANSI stripping only worked for streams exposing a `.buffer` (i.e. most real streams), but silently didn't apply for buffer-less streams like `StringIO` (the no-stdout fallback), so `color=False` had no effect there. Now stripping is applied consistently regardless of the underlying stream type. Updated `tests/test_termui.py` accordingly (fixed the test that had locked in the old buggy behavior, updated the fake-context-manager test to the new 2-tuple shape, and refreshed stale docstrings referencing `_has_binary_buffer`). Full test suite passes (1900 passed, 94 skipped).
